title: Combined FHL transfer and SpeedBridge reconstruction for calcific avulsion in insertional Achilles tendinopathy: a case report.
journal: International journal of surgery case reports

sections.label: INTRODUCTION AND IMPORTANCE
sections.text: Insertional Achilles tendinopathy (IAT) is a chronic degenerative condition characterized by pain and structural changes at the calcaneal insertion. Although conservative management remains first-line treatment, a substantial proportion of patients ultimately require surgical intervention. Several surgical strategies have been described for refractory IAT, including debridement, posterior calcaneal osteoplasty, tendon detachment with reinsertion using single- or double-row anchors, and augmentation techniques such as flexor hallucis longus (FHL) tendon transfer. Massive intratendinous calcifications complicated by acute avulsion at the tendon insertion are rare.

sections.label: PRESENTATION OF CASE
sections.text: A 52-year-old competitive handball player presented with acute posterior heel pain sustained during sport. Imaging revealed the avulsion of a large insertional calcific deposit associated with Achilles tendon rupture and poor-quality residual fibers. Surgical management consisted of extensive debridement, posterior calcaneal osteotomy, FHL tendon transfer, and double-row SpeedBridge fixation. At 24 months postoperatively, the patient had returned to competitive sport at his pre-injury level with excellent functional outcomes and no complications.

sections.label: CLINICAL DISCUSSION
sections.text: In cases of extensive tendon degeneration and calcific avulsion, primary repair alone may be insufficient. Combining biological augmentation with FHL transfer and mechanical reinforcement using double-row fixation may improve structural integrity and functional recovery.

sections.label: CONCLUSION
sections.text: Massive calcific avulsion with substantial tendon loss represents a severe form of insertional Achilles disease. In high-demand patients, combining FHL transfer with double-row fixation may restore tendon continuity and enable return to sport.
